habitat: Coffee mugs, T-shirts, and greeting cards — precisely the categories a court has already priced.
diet: Feeds on a single unchanging facial expression read as perpetual disapproval.
predators: One, decisively: a 2018 jury verdict of $710,001 against a defendant who had a licence and still exceeded it.
transmission: Static image macro; the face is recaptioned, never redrawn.
cause_of_death: The photographed cat died in 2019. The brand and the litigation precedent did not.
resurrection: None needed — the enforcement posture is now the specimen's most reproduced trait.
host_population: Anyone tempted to put the face on a physical product without checking who owns it first.
mutation: Minimal on the image itself; the surrounding case law is what keeps mutating, in the form of new cease-and-desist letters.
prognosis: Never pursue for merch, without exception. This is the register's own worked example of what happens when someone does.
underlying_work: Photograph of a cat, plus registered marks
enforcement_history: Jury verdict January 2018 totalling $710,001: $230,000 statutory copyright, $480,000 statutory trademark, $1 contract. Infringing goods were coffee and t-shirts.
curatorial_note: The clearest merch precedent in the whole register. The defendant even had a licence and still lost by exceeding it. Cite this case in the exhibit text.
